title: Principle 5: Retrieval: test to learn
coreMove: Force knowledge out from memory before looking again, so testing becomes learning rather than judgment.
sourcePressure: Retrieval means producing knowledge through recall instead of smoothing over weakness with passive rereading. The source sidecar contains no named people, studies, institutions, places, dates, or artifacts for this chapter, so named source anchors must be omitted rather than invented.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Framing retrieval as exam anxiety, trivia, or punishment instead of a way to expose what the page was hiding.

hook: Ch8: learner stares at browser tabs and realizes motivation is not enough
Ch8: broad modern world pressure opener

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Megan, a board presenter closing the slide deck to recall the case
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan turns the board deck face down and writes the acquisition case from memory before checking the slide order.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a darkened projector screen above a closed presentation remote

exampleSpecs.domain: Sam, a history seminar student explaining an argument with the book shut
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam explains the history argument to a classmate with the book shut and marks the point where recognition disappears.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paperback face down beside an empty seminar mug

exampleSpecs.domain: Chiara, a paramedic trainee using face-down cards for drug doses
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chiara answers drug-dose cards from the back first, then sorts the failed ones into tonight's practice pile.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of face-down dose cards on an ambulance training cot

exampleSpecs.domain: Pavel, a software apprentice covering margin hints before solving again
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the project survives contact with a real schedule and real standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pavel covers the margin hints and rebuilds the software solution from the problem statement alone.

exampleSpecs.domain: Hadiya, a law student writing questions before reopening the casebook
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether comfort keeps protecting the exact skill gap that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hadiya writes three casebook questions before rereading so the next pass has to answer a demand from memory.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a legal pad headed with questions beside a closed casebook

exampleSpecs.domain: Lars, a chemistry tutor rewriting prompts that give away the answer
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next attempt changes the skill instead of decorating the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars rewrites a chemistry quiz so the prompt no longer gives away the reagent before the student has to recall it.

skillTargets: recognize when familiarity is masquerading as knowledge

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
